artwork.subject: May broad beans
artwork.description: Edited 10:31.6 source crop with lifted deep shadows and three foreground pods referenced to the real crop at 11:30.
artwork.prompt: Make a very small photo edit to image 1, an exact square crop of John's real allotment video filmed 25 May 2026 at 10:31.6. Image 1 is the exact framing and complete site: preserve the real West boundary at its actual height and location, the clipped evergreen over only the left wall section, the timbers above the right blockwork, the little shed/roof glimpses behind the wall, the overhead cable, pale green shed corner and BLACK water butt right (same size and position), slab path and background beds, and the existing broad bean crop and tied bamboo exactly. Do not invent or relocate any boundary or structure, or change the framing. Put two or three clearly legible authentic edible broad bean pods attached at different heights within the near foliage, most visible in the left/centre part of the square (just above the front rail and below the upper leaves). Use the real pods from image 2 filmed in this SAME broad bean bed for anatomical scale, soft green seams, blunt-ended shape and how they attach at a node. The pods are substantial enough to read at 19 mm on a book page, one partly overlapped by real foliage. They are similar to actual pods in image 2, not repeated or gigantic, and not pea pods. Lift the deepest under-canopy shadows slightly without dulling real sunny May side light or making it HDR. Keep actual imperfections and real footage look. A single fully filled 1:1 image, no text, hands or people.

artwork.subject: Early-December Cavolo Nero
artwork.description: Reconstruction from the same 10:31.6 camera frame, adjusted slightly for viewpoint and season. Mature kale replaces beans and temporary supports.
artwork.prompt: Rephotograph image 1, the exact square 10:31.6 May video frame, on a damp overcast day in early December from an almost identical handheld standpoint on the slabs, only about a few inches to one side and a slight two or three degree left turn. This is for the second square on the facing spread, the same bed later in the year. Use IMAGE 1 as strict authority for the footprint, DEPTH and placement of all permanent real structures. In particular preserve its weathered west boundary block wall HALF WAY UP BACKGROUND behind the intervening beds, the distinct clipped conifer overhanging only the left/centre portion of the grey wall, the horizontal weathered boards on the top of the right section, bins beneath and rooflines behind. Do NOT draw a continuous hedge, taller new wall, or move any part of the background closer. The black water butt is at the extreme right very near the camera, attached to the pale green shed corner, just as in image 1. Keep the junction of the slab paving to the soil, the distant blue hoops or authentic small supports in neighbouring beds as supported by image 1. Image 2 from 18:00 in the same real video confirms the weathered masonry and overhanging trimmed conifer; its close framing is not the result. Maintain the same overall scale and recognisable landmarks with subtle perspective changes in slabs and foliage. Replace only the supported foreground broad bean row at lower LEFT (the open unframed soil left of slabs, not the background bed) with three to four visibly distinct fully established mature Cavolo Nero plants, one prominent in near left lower/central foreground, different sizes and silhouette. Use IMAGE 3 just as a reference for lifelike mature, partly harvested leaves, NOT FOR THE SITE, WALL, LANDMARKS, OR COMPOSITION. Each soil-rooted plant has a different lean and crown, matte blue-green strap leaves with distinct folds, irregular overlaps and hanging outer leaves, harvest scars down lower stalk, one aging pale lower leaf farther along and a tiny insect hole or two only. Do not exaggerate damage or make cloned rosettes. Remove ALL of the tall thin canes and horizontal front rails from the replaced broad bean row, other shorter supports clearly behind the bed may stay. Early December Cornwall is overcast in this image: a pale grey sky, subdued neutral daylight, damp nuanced soil, a few leaf scraps, more subdued neighbouring beds and seasonally sparse surrounding vegetation. The conifer stays green but darker. No snow, harsh shadows, strongly blue tint or summer sun. No people or text. One exact square fill photo with the natural detail and believable scale of a real home allotment.

video_scan.close_review: Sampled at one-second intervals or finer around the broad bean bed and shed turn, with selected west wall and roof checks.
